overview: ArcBest is a freight and logistics company offering integrated services across multiple transportation service lines. The goal was to consolidate tools across divisions into a single Transportation Management System (TMS) that reduces reliance on third-party systems and enhances internal efficiency.

sections.title: My Role
paragraphs: I led user research, stakeholder workshops, workflow mapping, and the definition of a unified design language. I also supported feature validation and UI delivery across multiple teams.

sections.title: What is a TMS?
paragraphs: A TMS manages data on loads, carriers, routes, costs, and contact info — providing a centralized view of freight movements and enabling planning, tracking, and coordination.

items: Partial Truckload (PT): Purchased capacity from 3rd party vendors
Less Than Truckload Brokerage (LTLB): Small shipments from multiple customers
Dedicated: Vehicles dedicated to single clients or contracts
Fragmented tools and inconsistent workflows across teams
Overlapping data and disconnected service line logic
Need for visual consistency and platform-wide design language
"A shipment is a shipment": Found significant overlap in load structure and lifecycle across service lines
Unified UI patterns: Required consistent interactions and interface elements
Multiple parallel projects: Influenced other ArcBest product teams to adopt shared language

features.name: Prioritized Action List
features.headline: Your tasks, organized.
features.description: A centralized task view for users to manage loads assigned by supervisors—eliminating redundancy and noise. Focus on what matters, ignore the rest.

features.name: Load Board
features.headline: Every load, at a glance.
features.description: Displays load lifecycle stages across service lines. Enables prioritization via quick filters based on location and operational status.

features.name: Load Details
features.headline: Deep dive, instantly.
features.description: Unified tabs for Stops, Commodities, Tracking, Carrier Details, Financials, and more. Everything about a load, organized and accessible in one place.

features.name: Manual Load Creation
features.headline: No EDI? No problem.
features.description: Enabled users to create loads manually via phone or email if not received through automated EDI feeds. Flexibility when automation falls short.

sections.title: Outcomes
items: Unified user experience across previously siloed teams
Improved visibility into operations and financials
Simplified onboarding for new service lines and workflows

sections.title: Reflections
paragraphs: This was a complex, multi-year systems integration challenge. Working across service lines meant aligning on terminology, workflows, and tools. Early wins came from shared visual patterns and consistent user research cadence. The design language helped bring cohesion and speed to a long roadmap of products.
